items.title: Global deforestation slowed in 2025 but surged in Congo basin: Study
items.summary: Deforestation slowed worldwide last year, but the improvement is unlikely to last as the situation deteriorates in Central Africa and an exceptionally strong El Niño weather pattern intensifies, a new study said on Wednesday.

items.title: Trailblazing technique uncovers real shape of scorching-hot exoplanet atmospheres
items.summary: Until now, the alien white-hot worlds of exoplanets have been depicted as circular, but new research has revealed the true shape of their atmospheres to be a deformed sphere rather than a perfect circle.

items.title: New knee arthritis treatment delivers lasting pain relief without surgery
items.summary: A promising new treatment for knee arthritis uses tiny, dissolvable particles to block abnormal blood vessels, easing inflammation and pain without joint replacement surgery. In a study of 194 patients, 80% experienced clinically meaningful pain relief lasting at least 12 months.

items.title: Wild bobwhite quail spotted after habitat restoration project
items.summary: Multiple coveys of wild bobwhite quail were recently sighted at the University of Tennessee's Ames AgResearch and Education Center, marking an encouraging milestone in an ongoing effort to restore habitat for the species at this historic bird dog field trial destination.

items.title: People with a 'good ear' for sounds make better language learners, study suggests
items.summary: People who are better at noticing fine details in sound—an ability known as auditory precision—can master the pronunciation of new languages faster and more accurately than other learners, a new study published in the Journal of Experimental Psychology finds.
